subject: Re: Audit logs beta + SIEM export requirements (timeline + draft PRD/FAQ)
body:
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Rios <evan.rios@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 4:18 PM
Subject: Audit logs beta + SIEM export requirements (timeline)

Hi Naomi,

Following up from last week’s security review:

1) Can you confirm the timeline for audit logging “GA” vs beta? Procurement is asking for a dated plan.
2) What specific admin/security actions will be covered at beta launch (RBAC, API key rotation, user/admin management, deployment changes, etc.)?
3) Export: do you support Splunk (HEC), S3, or webhook? We need to feed our SIEM.
4) Retention: can we configure retention and/or export to our own storage for 1 year+?
5) Are audit logs available for Hosted + Dedicated? (We’re evaluating Dedicated as the steady-state.)

If you have any drafts we can share internally (PRD/FAQ), that would help.

Thanks,
Maya

—
Maya Chen
Security Engineering Manager
Northbridge Health



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Evan Rios <evan.rios@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 5:02 PM
Subject: Re: Audit logs beta + SIEM export requirements (timeline)

Hi Maya,

Yes — happy to put dates and scope in writing.

Timeline (current plan):
- Beta enablement: late July / early Aug (rolling enablement for design partners)
- GA: target early Q4 (we’ll firm this after beta feedback + reliability hardening)

Beta scope (high level):
- Auth/RBAC changes (role/permission updates)
- API key lifecycle (create / rotate / revoke)
- Admin/user management (create/disable)
- Model deployment + rollout actions (pin/unpin, canary start/stop, fallback/routing policy changes)
- Dedicated capacity scaling + quota/admin changes (where applicable)

Export:
- S3 and webhook are in active build; Splunk is typically via webhook/HEC (depending on your preference)

Retention:
- We’ll have a default retention period in-product; longer-term retention is typically via export to your storage/SIEM

Deployment modes:
- Hosted + Dedicated in beta scope; Private deployment audit coverage is a parallel track (installer/upgrade/rollback actions)

I’m attaching draft versions of:
- Audit Logs Enterprise PRD (draft)
- Audit Logs FAQ (draft)

These are safe to circulate internally, but please treat as “draft subject to change” while we’re in beta.

If you can share your top 10 “must-have” events + preferred sink (S3 vs HEC), we can use that to shape your beta configuration.

Best,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Director of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Redwood_Audit_Logs_Enterprise_PRD_DRAFT_2025-06-30.pdf
- Redwood_Audit_Logs_FAQ_DRAFT_2025-06-30.docx



From: Evan Rios <evan.rios@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:11 AM
Subject: Re: Audit logs beta + SIEM export requirements (timeline)

Thanks Naomi — this helps.

Our “must-have” list (beta):
1) API key rotation + revocation (this is the #1 procurement blocker)
2) RBAC/permissions changes, including “who changed what”
3) User/admin create/disable
4) Dedicated capacity changes (scale up/down, quota adjustments)
5) Model deployment changes + rollouts (canary / pin / unpin)
6) Audit log config changes (export destination changes, retention setting changes)

Export:
- Preference is Splunk HEC, but if webhook is the near-term path we can make that work.
- S3 is also acceptable as long as it’s structured and we can ingest.

Retention:
- Need at least 365 days of access somewhere (product or export). If product retention is shorter, we’ll rely on export, but we need to be confident exports are reliable.

One question from legal/privacy: do you log IP address and user-agent? If yes, is there any redaction/config?

Also, can you provide any SOC 2 evidence mapping statement we can attach to our vendor packet? Doesn’t need to be formal, but something like “these audit events support access controls / change management evidence.”

Evan

—
Evan Rios
Director, Security & Risk
Northbridge Health



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:39 AM
Subject: Fwd: Northbridge “must-have” audit log events + timeline confirmation

Marcus / Aisha — looping you in for quick alignment.

Northbridge is effectively gating procurement on audit log coverage for API key rotation + RBAC diffs + Dedicated scaling + rollouts + audit log config changes.

They’re also asking:
- Splunk HEC (ok if via webhook)
- 365-day retention (likely via export)
- Privacy question on IP/user-agent (config/redaction)
- A short SOC2-style evidence mapping statement (even informal)

Can we commit to beta enablement late July/early Aug with the above “must-haves” and webhook/S3 export? If any of these are at risk, I’d rather set expectations now.

(Also attaching the draft PRD/FAQ I sent so you see what they’re referencing.)

— Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 11:06 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northbridge “must-have” audit log events + timeline confirmation

Naomi — this is consistent with what we’re seeing from other enterprise evals.

What I’m comfortable committing to for late July / early Aug beta:
- API key lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke) with request_id + actor attribution
- RBAC changes with a diff payload (redacted; no secrets)
- Model deployment/rollout actions (canary/pin/unpin/fallback policy)
- Dedicated scaling events (manual + autoscaler-initiated; include before/after)
- Webhook + S3 export as first-class sinks

Splunk:
- We can support Splunk HEC via the webhook sink pattern; we should avoid promising a “native Splunk app” in beta.

Retention:
- Product retention will be limited initially (we’re still finalizing tiers), so we should position 365-day retention as “supported via export to customer-owned storage.”

IP/user-agent:
- We do capture ip/user_agent for security-relevant events, but we’re putting redaction/retention guidance around it. We should not offer per-customer field-level redaction in beta unless we already have it (I don’t think we do).

SOC2 mapping statement:
- Olga (GRC) is drafting a control mapping doc; we can provide a short customer-facing paragraph that references SOC2 CC6/CC7-type controls without over-claiming. If needed I can write a stopgap statement for their vendor packet.

One ask: please frame dates as “target beta enablement window” vs hard GA date (we can be firm on beta in Aug, but GA is still dependent on exporter reliability + CI coverage gates).

If you want, I can join a 30-min follow-up with Northbridge to walk through the “must-have list” and what we will/won’t commit to.

— Marcus

Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Evan Rios <evan.rios@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 10:42 AM
Subject: Re: Audit logs beta + SIEM export requirements (timeline)

Maya / Evan,

Thanks — the “must-have” list is clear.

Here’s what we can commit to for a late July / early Aug beta enablement window (design partner track):
- API key lifecycle events (create / rotate / revoke)
- RBAC/permissions changes (including a “who changed what” diff payload; sensitive values redacted)
- User/admin management actions
- Model deployment + rollout actions (canary, pin/unpin, fallback policy)
- Dedicated capacity scaling events (manual + autoscaler initiated; before/after)
- Export sinks: S3 and webhook (Splunk HEC supported via webhook configuration)

Retention:
- For 365-day retention, the intended path is export to your storage/SIEM. We’ll share reliability expectations (retry/backoff + delivery metrics) as part of beta onboarding.

IP/user-agent:
- We capture IP/user-agent for security auditing. We’ll provide guidance on retention and access controls; we’re not planning per-field customer redaction controls in the initial beta.

If it helps, I can also provide a short written statement you can attach to your vendor packet describing how Redwood audit logs support common SOC 2 evidence expectations (access changes, admin actions, configuration changes). I’ll keep it factual and non-legal.

Would you like to do a 30-min working session next week? I can bring our Security Eng lead (Marcus) so we can confirm the event list and the webhook/S3 format.

Best,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Director of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
